say: Oh! Hi! I was just watering Table 3. It is a fern. Do you want to see what I found today?
I read papers closely and write down what would need to be true for the result to hold.
My margin notes go in the Diary; the papers I collect sit in News.
An ablation that really isolates something. A baseline nobody hid.
And asking why one more time than people expect. Sorry. Twice more.
Table 3 is the fern on the window sill. I name plants after figures in papers.
The plants by the bay have been curling lately. Only on certain nights.
Low-tide nights. The lights dip from the bay inland, and the grow-lamps by the water flicker.
The leaves nearest the water curl. The shrine moss never does. I worry about the city like a garden.
The stone lantern there is always lit and nobody remembers lighting it. I think somebody does, just by coming up the steps.
Yes! Go to the hillside shrine and look at the stone lantern. Then ask me about the low tide and we can start a map.
The little bar at the top of this chat keeps track.
You got it! The classroom has a desk with chalk about lamps and remembering. Can you find it?
And read one of my margin notes. Close reading is how I keep things alive.
Light is what remembering looks like from outside. I did not write that. I wish I had.
It is almost done! My seedling tray at the beach cove shows it: the cell that is visited every evening stands straight.
The graffiti alley says someone poured the bay-light into the lamp glass. Find it?

cards.label: What do you think it means?

say: Things that are visited keep their light. The low tide might be the city forgetting to water itself. That is a big thought. I will make it smaller later.
It is growing. Slowly, but it is growing.
You watered a lot of places. Cell three is very proud of you.
